newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee rebounds, July regains $2,100.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee rebounds, July regains $2,100.

text.p: Nearby LIFFE coffee futures rebounded in late Tuesday trade with July regaining a foothold above the $2,100 a tonne mark, spurred by roaster buying amid a new rally in New York.
The London market had been kept on the downside throughout the morning and in early afternoon on origin selling.
But the rise on the back of small volume was far from impressive in relation to New York's arabica futures.
The day's volume was 4,755 lots was mainly dominated by jobbers. Of that, 500 lots were against actual trades.
Benchmark July rebounded from a low of $2,065 to finish the day at $2,101 a tonne, up $15 on the day and just $1 off its day's peak.
The second-month position had risen to a high of $2,190 on May 15 after breaching the $2,100 mark for the first time since January 1996.
September posted the biggest rise at $22 to finish at $2,120. In switches, July/Sept spread stood at $19 at the close while Sept/Nov was at level money.
New York's July hit a new life-of-contract high of 269.50 cents a lb in Tuesday morning trade on local and speculative buying. By 1627 GMT, the contract was 10.35 cents up 267.20 cents.
Immediately, LIFFE's July is seen supported at $2,050. Traders said the current uptrend remained intact if July holds above $1,900.
On the upside, the main technical goal is $2,145, followed by the May 19 peak of $2,190.
The market was closed on Monday for a local holiday.
Generally, players are keeping a cautious stance in view of the current Brazilian cold season.
There was no damaging cold in Brazil's coffee belt over the weekend and no freeze was forecast for the rest of this week.
"But everybody wants to play safe now," another said.
The last severe frosts in 1994, one in June and another in July, damaged some Brazil's coffee trees and sent world prices spiralling.

The private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said in an update on Tuesday an intensifying storm system along the south coast of Brazil could drive cooler air up into the coffee belt later this week and over the weekend.
However, the airmass is not expected to cause any damage, it said.
In other news, Japan's coffee stocks rose by a sharp 22.7 percent year on year to 67,298 tonnes in April as roasters rebuilt their low inventories following the steep price rally since January.
